aiOverview.content: "Real" describes something actually existing, genuine, or not artificial. It commonly means true, authentic, or tangible (not imaginary). Synonyms include actual, genuine, true, authentic, and tangible. Antonyms include fake, artificial, imaginary, fictitious, and unreal. It is used to describe tangible items, accurate information, or to mean "very" in informal English. Contextual Usage Objects: "Real leather," "real flowers" (not artificial). Situations/Truth: "Real life," "a real possibility" (existing in fact). Emphasis (Adverb): "Real good time," "real easy" (meaning very). Finance/Economics: "Real earnings" (adjusted for inflation), "real estate" (property). Currency: The Brazilian real (plural: reais). EtymologyThe word stems from the Latin reālis ("actual"), which is derived from res ("thing"). It has also historically referred to a Spanish silver coin (real). Common Phrases For real: Honestly, truly, or seriously. The real McCoy: The genuine article. Real estate: Property consisting of land or buildings. Real time: The actual time during which a process occurs. Synonyms and Antonyms Synonyms: Actual, authentic, bona fide, certain, genuine, honest, legitimate, material, physical, sincere, substantive, tangible, true. Antonyms: Artificial, bogus, fake, false, fictional, imaginary, insincere, mock, nominal, pretended, unreal.
